articles.title: Champions League draw: Mourinho’s quest for number 16 begins against Inter, Arsenal and Leipzig
articles.standfirst: Breaking down Real Madrid’s eight Champions League opponents
articles.summary: Breaking down Real Madrid’s eight Champions League opponents
articles.body:
R eal Madrid already know who they will face on their European road to the Sixteenth . The draw held today in Monaco handed the Whites a total of eight opponents for the 2026/27 Champions League league phase , four of them at the Santiago Bernabéu and four others away from home.

The competition also carries a special added incentive on the bench. José Mourinho faces his first Champions League of this second spell with an old unfinished score to settle: the Big Eared trophy eluded him in his first stint at Real Madrid, when he reached three consecutive semifinals without making the final . The Portuguese coach, who has lifted the trophy with other clubs, is now looking to settle that debt and return Madrid to the summit of a tournament the club considers its natural habitat.

Real Madrid's Champions League opponents

The draw was decided with the 36 participants split into four pots according to the UEFA coefficient, so that each team faces two opponents from each pot, one at home and one away. Madrid, placed in the first pot, could not be drawn against other Spanish clubs nor face more than two teams from the same country . The dates and kick-off times for each matchday will be announced over the weekend.

When does Real Madrid play in the Champions League?

Although Real Madrid already knows the names of its first eight opponents and knows which ones it will play against at the Santiago Bernabéu and which ones it will have to visit, there is still no schedule . UEFA will make it public over the weekend, and that will be the time to book tickets for the away matches and seats for the clashes at the Whites' home ground.

The format maintains the structure introduced in previous editions. The 36 teams share a single standings table: the top eight advance directly to the round of 16, while those placed between ninth and twenty-fourth play an intermediate two-legged round . The rest are eliminated, with no Europa League safety net. From the round of 16 onward, the tournament returns to its traditional knockout format through to the final, which this season will be played in its own city, on June 5, 2027 at the Metropolitano stadium.

Old acquaintances, rematches and a debut

The most storied clash will undoubtedly be that with Inter . The two giants have faced each other 19 times throughout history, with Madrid holding the upper hand (ten victories), although the Italians retain a painful episode for Madridismo. They were the executioners in the 1964 final , one of the few finals the club has lost. The reunion also has a special flavor for Mourinho , who won his second Champions League precisely with Inter , in 2010 and on the pitch at the Bernabéu . Recent meetings, however, have smiled on Madrid, who came out on top in both group-stage encounters in 2021/22.

More recent and tinged with revenge is the meeting with Arsenal . The Gunners eliminated Madrid in the quarter-finals of 2024/25 with a convincing 5-1 aggregate scoreline (3-0 at the Emirates, with a Declan Rice brace, and 2-1 at the Bernabéu), in one of the most bitter nights from two seasons ago. Los Blancos, now under Mourinho, will have the chance to make amends for that drubbing.

Roma also falls into the category of familiar old foes. The two teams have crossed paths repeatedly in the present century, always in the top competition, with their last meeting coming in the 2015/16 round of 16 , settled in Madrid's favor. Something similar applies to PSV and Shakhtar Donetsk , recent group-stage opponents against whom the club in white usually comes out on top, although the Ukrainian side — which will play its home matches at Stamford Bridge — has already pulled off a surprise or two, such as the 3-2 win it inflicted at Valdebebas in 2020/21.

Special mention goes to RB Leipzig , whom Madrid already faced in the group stage of 2022/23, and who now reappear with added intrigue: from their ranks comes the most expensive signing in the club's history, Yan Diomande . The list is completed by two exotic opponents: AEK Athens , a very rare matchup, and Austria's LASK , a completely new opponent in the club's European history. Two almost or entirely unprecedented scenarios for a Madrid side that, as always, starts with the status of favorite in its eternal pursuit of the Sixteenth.

articles.title: Blockbuster draw! Defending champions PSG set for epic clashes with Manchester City and Barcelona
articles.standfirst: Will they be able to dethrone the champion?
articles.summary: Will they be able to dethrone the champion?
articles.body:
Two-time defending champion Paris Saint-Germain will host Manchester City and travel to Barcelona in the Champions League main phase this season, after the 36-team draw was made Thursday.

PSG has won three straight visits to Barcelona — including a 2-1 win in the league phase last October — since imploding in the famous 6-1 loss in March 2017 that is known as the “ Remontada ” game.

The French champion again plays Aston Villa , after a Super Cup win this month, and goes to Champions League newcomer Como, coached by Cesc Fabregas , in an eight-game slate that starts in two weeks' time.

Real Madrid will host Inter Milan and make two trips to London, at Arsenal and against Shakhtar Donetsk . Ukraine’s champion is playing home games at Stamford Bridge, where Madrid's returning coach José Mourinho was beloved by Chelsea fans in a pair of title-winning spells there.

Barcelona will host two English clubs — Man City and Europa League winner Villa — plus its former player Fabregas with Como. A long trip to Azerbaijan awaits to face debutant Sabah in Baku.

Arsenal, the beaten finalist last year, will host Madrid, Borussia Dortmund and Sabah , and travel to Bayern Munich.

Bayern got a second English opponent, with a trip to Manchester United, plus two Norwegian opponents, hosting Bodø/Glimt and visiting Viking. Bayern also will go to Atletico Madrid whose Metropolitano Stadium will host the final next May.

Liverpool got trips to Inter Milan and Fenerbahce in what looked one of the more favorable slates of eight games. Atletico will again come to Anfield where Liverpool won 3-2 last September.

Atletico also will play both Norwegian teams and is one of four teams heading inside the Arctic Circle to play on Bodø/Glimt ’s artificial turf. Dortmund, Lille and newcomer LASK also will travel to the remote fishing town, and one team must make the trip in January.

Sabah also will host Dortmund, Napoli and Slavia Prague . Fans also have two long trips from Azerbaijan to England to face Arsenal and Man United.

Como has a second trip to Spain, to play Real Betis as well as Barcelona, and will welcome PSG and Man United to its picture-postcard lakeside stadium home.

Four debutants in Champions League draw

Four newcomers will debut in this Champions League edition: Como from Italy, coached by Cesc Fabregas; LASK of Austria; Viking from Norway; and Azerbaijani champion Sabah , which was founded only in 2017.

Sabah coach Valdas Dambrauskas is already making headlines for his curious origin story in soccer. The money he won as a young contestant on TV quiz show “ Who Wants to be a Millionaire ” in his native Lithuania funded a trip to study coaching in England.

Another first this season is an African coach taking his team into the main phase. Former Manchester City and Barcelona star Yaya Touré guided Slovakian champion Slovan Bratislava through its qualifying playoff Wednesday. Slovan will visit PSG and host Inter Milan .

Champions League draw details

UEFA’s draw software allocated eight opponents to each team — four home games, four away — with two opponents taken from each seeding pot. Seeding was decided by ranking a team's European results over the past five years. Teams could not be paired with an opponent from their own country.

The first round of games is played Sept. 8-10 with the first six rounds played through December. The league phase resumes in January with the eighth and final round on Jan. 27 .

The top eight teams in the final standings go direct to the round of 16 in March. Teams placed ninth to 24th enter the knockout playoffs in February to decide the other eight teams in the round of 16. Teams placed 25th to 36th are eliminated .

The 36 teams will share prize money of about 2.5 billion euros ($2.9 billion).

articles.title: Real Madrid and Barcelona: Who came out better after the 2026/27 Champions League draw?
articles.standfirst: The road to one of Europe’s biggest titles is beginning to take shape, and the two Spanish giants will not face the same challenge.
articles.summary: The road to one of Europe’s biggest titles is beginning to take shape, and the two Spanish giants will not face the same challenge.
articles.body:
The 2026 World Cup is now part of the past, but international soccer has a new story waiting to be written. This time, the spotlight returns to the clubs, with the Champions League beginning to reveal some of the matchups that could shape the season.

Real Madrid and Barcelona now know the eight teams they will face in the league phase of the 2026/27 edition , following Thursday’s draw in Monaco. And while it is still far too early to talk about favorites, simply looking at the names on their respective schedules reveals a difference that immediately stands out.

While one team will have to prepare to host Inter and travel to Arsenal, the other will face Manchester City, PSG and a difficult trip to Galatasaray .

The question, then, almost asks itself: who got the easier path?

Real Madrid already know their eight opponents

The Merengue side, led by José Mourinho , will play four matches at home and four away during this opening stage of the Champions League.

At home, they will face Inter, PSV, RB Leipzig and LASK . The matchup against the Italian side stands out as the biggest challenge of the four, although playing in front of their own fans could give Real Madrid an opportunity to collect valuable points from the start.

Things will look different on the road. Arsenal, Roma, Shakhtar Donetsk and AEK Athens will be their away opponents, with the trip to face the English side emerging as one of the matches likely to attract the most attention.

Barcelona have several big nights ahead

Barcelona, meanwhile, will begin the competition with several opponents capable of immediately raising the difficulty of their schedule.

At home, they will welcome Manchester City, Aston Villa, Feyenoord and Como . Among those matches, the clash with Pep Guardiola’s side stands out as one of the biggest attractions of the league phase.

Hansi Flick’s team will travel to face PSG, Sporting CP, Galatasaray and Sabah . And one match inevitably stands above the rest: their trip to Paris to take on the reigning European champions.

The matchup will also have an added layer of intrigue, as the two teams will meet again after their clash last season.

So, when it comes to who received the easier path, Real Madrid appear to have been handed a slightly more favorable route than Barcelona .

However, the draw is only the starting point. The real answer will come once the ball starts rolling and each opponent stops being just a name on a schedule and becomes a test capable of shaping the course of an entire season.

articles.standfirst: UEFA published this Saturday all the schedules for the eight matchdays
articles.summary: UEFA published this Saturday all the schedules for the eight matchdays
articles.body:
UEFA published this Saturday the schedules for the eight matchdays of the Champions League league phase. In other words, the five Spanish teams ( Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atlético, Villarreal and Betis ) already know when and against whom they will play in each of the matchdays.

Thus, Real Madrid will make their debut against Inter at home (21:00) on Tuesday, September 8, Barcelona against Feyenoord also at home (18:45) on Wednesday, September 9, Atlético will visit Anfield (21:00) on Wednesday, September 9, Villarreal will play against Dortmund away (21:00) on Tuesday, September 8, and Betis against Lille away from home (21:00) on Tuesday, September 8.

After the draw held last Thursday, in which each team learned who their eight opponents would be, it remained to find out the times and dates on which they will face each of them. The matchday dates, which were already known, are as follows:

Matchday 1: September 8–10, 2026

Matchday 2: October 13/14, 2026

Matchday 3: October 20/21, 2026

Matchday 4: November 3/4, 2026

Matchday 5: November 24/25, 2026

Matchday 6: 8/9 December 2026

Matchday 7: January 19/20, 2027

Matchday 8: January 27, 2027

Playoff dates and matchups

As in previous years, the top eight teams in the league phase will qualify directly for the round of 16. The teams placed between ninth and twenty-fourth will play a playoff from which the other eight round-of-16 qualifiers will emerge. This playoff will be played on February 16/17 (the first-leg matches) and February 23/24 (the second-leg matches) in 2027.

Round of 16: March 9/10 and 16/17, 2027

Quarter-finals: April 6/7 and 13/14, 2027

Semi-finals: April 27/28 and May 4/5, 2027

articles.title: Mourinho's Champions League with Real Madrid: The Final Chapter
articles.standfirst: The coach has a second chance to settle the continental debt that remained outstanding after his first spell on the Madrid bench
articles.summary: The coach has a second chance to settle the continental debt that remained outstanding after his first spell on the Madrid bench
articles.body:
Mourinho fell short of the Tenth with Real Madrid and now will fight for the Sixteenth . His return is a second chance to settle a debt with the Champions League that remained unfinished after his first spell on the Madrid bench. He came close to it, after three consecutive lost semifinals , but did not lift it. Even so, Florentino Pérez himself has acknowledged that, even without winning it, Mou put Madrid on the path to all the Champions Leagues that would come afterward. Specifically, six: three with Zidane and three with Ancelotti . In fact, the Tenth would arrive in Real Madrid's trophy cabinet in the very season after the Portuguese coach's departure.

Mourinho left Madrid with the thorn of not winning the Champions League still stuck in him , but what he did do was restore Madrid to the place it rightfully belonged in Europe, a place from which it had drifted away alarmingly. When Mou arrived at Real Madrid, the club had lost all its European magic after suffering six consecutive round-of-16 eliminations . After being knocked out in the quarter-finals in 03-04, Madrid went through a continental nightmare it could not escape. Until 2010, it kept piling up Champions League disasters one after another. Round of 16, round of 16, round of 16, round of 16, round of 16, round of 16... The wall was impassable for them.

Obviously, I’m excited about winning the Champions League with Real Madrid

A leap in the Champions League without the final icing on the cake

And then Mourinho arrived, having just been crowned European champion against Bayern after eliminating Guardiola and Messi's all-powerful Barcelona in the semifinals . With the Portuguese in charge, Madrid regained its greatness in Europe. In his first season, they reached the semifinals unbeaten, with a record of eight wins and one draw . In the semis, Madrid came up against Barça and were eliminated after losing in Madrid and drawing in Barcelona. In the second attempt, Madrid got off to a flying start: six straight wins for a total of nine victories and one draw up to the semifinals . Mou once again took the team unbeaten to the penultimate step of the Champions League. Then it was Bayern who knocked Los Blancos out of the title race in a penalty shootout that went down in Madrid's dark history, with Cristiano, Kaká and Ramos missing three of the four spot kicks before elimination. And the third time was not the charm either. In Mourinho's final year as Real Madrid manager in his first spell, Madrid once again mounted a title challenge and reached the semifinals for the third consecutive year. But then Dortmund were Mou's executioners, as he saw the dream of winning the long-awaited Tenth slip away.

The saddest moment of my career was the Champions League elimination against Bayern, we were the best team in Europe

Now the Portuguese once again stands before the challenge of reconquering the Champions League for Real Madrid . Madrid has moved away from the title over the last two years after a golden era in which it dominated Europe with historic authority . And with the aim of returning to that triumphant period, Mourinho has come back, with a second chance to settle the unfinished business he has with the Champions League at Madrid.

A title that would also multiply his continental glory as a coach. Winning the Sixteenth with Madrid would mean Mou joining the exclusive club of coaches with three Champions League titles, where Paisley, Zidane, Guardiola and Luis Enrique are right now. In addition, he would be the only coach in history to win the European Cup with three different teams . And, as if that were not enough, he would also be the coach to win it with the longest gap since the last time. 17 years would have passed since he won the Champions League with Inter in 2010, surpassing the 15 years that separated Heynckes 's Champions League with Madrid in 1998 and the one he won with Bayern in 2013.

articles.body:
The Champions League , along with the World Cup , has become the great showcase of the "football planet" . Many young players each season look to leave their mark.

That is why at MARCA, to celebrate the start of the 2026-27 season, we wanted to select 10 prospects from outside LaLiga who could make a big splash in this edition. We have chosen ten players from 10 different teams to encourage diversity, all of them born on or after January 1, 2004 .

Nico Paz (Como/Argentina)

Position : Attacking midfielder. Age : 21 years old. Height : 1.85. Foot : Left-footed.

Como is making its debut... but the Spanish-Argentine already even knows what it is to score in the Champions League . He made his debut as a goalscorer in 2023 , at 19 years old, in Real Madrid's victory over Napoli (4-2) . Now he returns transformed into the star of Cesc's side and with the backing provided by the 20 goals and 17 assists he has recorded in 78 matches in "calcio". "The way we build our play is designed so that the ball reaches him in a certain way in every match," says Cesc . On the edge of the box he is lethal. He possesses a deadly shot from mid-range and great vision.

Rodrigo Mora (Roma/Portugal)

Position : Attacking midfielder . Age: 19 years old. Height: 1.68. Foot : Right-footed.

The " golden boy " of Porto did not fit into Francesco Farioli 's system and was forced to leave Do Dragao . The youngest player (17 years and 7 months) to score and assist in the same match for the "dragons" headed to Rome for a fee of 25 million. "He plays a kind of football that people love," said his former coach Vítor Bruno. He is not the strongest, but he has a low center of gravity that makes him terribly elusive . He turns well, changes direction easily and accelerates quickly. He has elegance to spare... but he lacks consistency.

Jérémy Jacquet (Liverpool/France)

Position : Centre-back. Age : 21 years old. Height : 1.90. Foot: Right-footed.

The former Rennes player, signed in January for 63.6 million euros , has become Van Dijk 's partner following Konaté departure to Real Madrid. "I know what my potential is," says Jacquet when asked about comparisons with Saliba . Charging forward, in full stride, he is a "bison". He has very long legs that help him win the ball easily and a great jumping ability that makes him difficult to beat in aerial duels . “He is still very young, I think he has all the qualities we will need for that position", maintains Andoni Iraola.

Konstantinos Karetsas (Borussia Dortmund/Greece)

Position : Attacking midfielder. Age: 18 years old. Height : 1.73. Preferred foot: Left-footed.

Borussia Dortmund has paid 30 million euros to Genk for this clone of Arda Güler. The Greek international possesses a "magic" left foot. Last season, without going any further, he recorded three goals and no fewer than 18 assists in 49 matches. "With his creativity and intelligence, he will enrich our team. He is very technically gifted and has the ability to find quick solutions in tight spaces," stressed Ole Book, the new sporting director of "BVB", by way of introduction. "He is a genuine old-school '10'," emphasizes his former coach Thorsten Fink.

Mika Godts (Paris Saint-Germain /Belgium)

Position : Winger. Age : 21 years old. Height : 1.76. Preferred foot : Right-footed.

A very different profile from Barcola . The new signing of Luis Enrique, who arrived from Ajax for 45 million euros , is already being compared in Belgium to Eden Hazard: right-footed , although he usually plays on the left; he is technically gifted, can go either way... The Eredivisie had become too small for him: he recorded 17 goals and 15 assists in 44 matches . "Some call it arrogance, but Mika exudes confidence. His dribbling is fantastic . He drives everyone crazy. Mika, in form, is a nightmare for any defender," says his former coach Hans Somers .

Robin Risser (Lens / France)

Position: Goalkeeper. Age : 21 years old. Height : 1.93. Foot: Right-footed.

One of the main "culprits" behind Lens winning the Cup and Super Cup... and finishing second in Ligue 1 . It's no surprise that Deschamps took him to the World Cup . Risser fits the profile of a modern goalkeeper . Very lanky (1.93 meters), he is comfortable between the posts and proves very consistent against point-blank shots . It is true that he often parries rather than catches . "He is very good on his line, he is good at managing depth, he is good with his feet and he is also good at coming off his line for aerial balls ," says his former coach Pierre Sage .

Johan Manzambi (Aston Villa / Switzerland)

Position : Midfielder. Age : 20 years old. Height : 1.82 m. Foot : Right-footed.

The former Freiburg player, signed for 60 million euros , was recently named "Best Young Player" of the Europa League and has emerged as one of the breakout stars of the World Cup . Manzambi, who scored seven goals and provided nine assists last season, stands out for his tremendous work rate. He can play in any position along the central axis (holding midfielder, central midfielder, box-to-box midfielder, attacking midfielder...) or out on the left . "He is a street footballer, one of those who need freedom . You've already seen it: he can press, has good dribbling ability, and knows how to finish,” says Murat Yakin . In the final stretch of the season, he especially developed his ability to get into attacking positions.

Ayyoub Bouaddi (Manchester City /Morocco)

Position: Midfielder. Age: 18 years old. Height : 1.85. Preferred foot: Right-footed.

Morocco's "6" was the first big proper name of the World Cup. "I was hugely impressed . How the lad plays! Barely 18 years old and so much football. He was everywhere on the pitch, moving, creating plays, breaking things up . If he keeps this up, this kid will go far," said Romário after the 1-1 against Brazil . For now, he has arrived at Manchester City, which has paid 95 million to Lille to make him the biggest transfer abroad in the history of Ligue 1 . An all-action midfielder. His build -he stands 1.86 metres tall- and physique are reminiscent of Guendouzi . He likes to play vertically, although he needs to start "producing" numbers. With the "dogues" he did not score. He only recorded four assists in 96 matches.

Lennart Karl (Bayern/Germany)

Position : Winger. Age : 18 years old. Height: 1.68. Foot : Left-footed.

The Bayern youth product is so young that he has not even been included in the "A list" for the Champions League . Last season he already made his mark. Only Lamine Yamal (10) surpassed him in goals produced in the Champions League (4) before turning 18 . He grew up admiring Odegaard while "polishing" himself as an attacking midfielder , but he also shines playing as an inverted winger . "I'm very quick over the first few meters, I like 1-on-1s and I can finish . I'm a little under 1.70 meters tall, I'm not the tallest, but my low center of gravity helps me dribble" , says Karl himself.

Victor Froholdt (Porto/Denmark)

Position : Midfielder. Age : 20 years old. Height : 1.87. Foot : Right-footed.

His "box-to-box" condition -he has great back-and-forth ability- makes him an ideal footballer for Farioli . He has the legs to guarantee the high press and high-intensity runs demanded by Porto's "futebol" . He doesn't just win the ball back. He also gets forward. Last season, without going any further, he recorded eight goals and seven assists . "Technically, this is where I can improve the most. If I manage to develop this, I will be able to use my strength, interception ability, and long-range ball control to create danger, make chances, and score goals," points out Froholdt . "He has an incredible "engine." He is capable of repeating high-intensity actions , this is something unique," underlines Farioli.

articles.title: 90 minutes that made history: Who is the first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League?
articles.standfirst: Zion Suzuki, Aston Villa's goalkeeper, became the first Japanese footballer to tend goal in a UEFA Champions League match.
articles.summary: Zion Suzuki, Aston Villa's goalkeeper, became the first Japanese footballer to tend goal in a UEFA Champions League match.
articles.body:
Zion Suzuki made history in Japanese football this Tuesday. The Aston Villa goalkeeper became the first Japanese goalkeeper to play minutes in the UEFA Champions League , starting in the match against Club Brugge on the opening matchday of the league phase.

The Japanese player played the full 90 minutes in the English side's 3-2 victory, in a match that had Aston Villa as the protagonist from the start and ended with a narrow win despite the Belgian team's reaction. The goalkeeper was crucial with his interventions to preserve the lead in the final stretch.

A record for Japanese football

At 24 years old, and following his recent arrival at Aston Villa, the Japan national team goalkeeper is thus taking on a new challenge in his career. UEFA includes him in the Aston Villa squad for the 2026/27 edition, and he has already recorded his first appearance in the top European club competition.

The debut could not have been more significant: in addition to becoming a pioneer for his country, Suzuki was part of a victory that allowed Aston Villa to begin their European campaign with three points.

Aston Villa got off on the right foot

The English side had an intense start and managed to take the lead in the 11th minute thanks to John McGinn . Bruges reacted quickly and found the equalizer, but the English team struck again before the half-hour mark, this time through Emiliano Buendía , to regain the lead.

Towards the end of the first half, Nicolas Jackson appeared to make it 3-1. The striker took advantage of a mistake by the Club Brugge goalkeeper and finished into an open net, thus scoring his first official goal wearing the Aston Villa shirt.

In the second half, Bruges came out determined to go for the game and managed to pull one back from the penalty spot in the 61st minute. The 3-2 scoreline added suspense to the final stretch, but the side managed by Unai Emery withstood the pressure and secured an important victory. In the midst of that closing stage, Zion Suzuki also had his moment under the crossbar and completed a historic night with a win on his Champions. debut.

articles.title: Real Madrid is ruthless in the Champions League
articles.standfirst: Courtois goalkeeper's saves nullify Inter's dominance on the field. The Whites, lacking a midfield presence, capitalize on the pressure and the Italians' mistakes.
articles.summary: Courtois goalkeeper's saves nullify Inter's dominance on the field. The Whites, lacking a midfield presence, capitalize on the pressure and the Italians' mistakes.
articles.body: K ylian Mbappe and Erling Haaland are off the mark in the Champions League as Real Madrid and Manchester City kicked off their campaigns with wins Tuesday. Mbappe gave record 15-time champion Madrid an early lead en route to 2-1 victory over Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabeu. Haaland scored both goals as 2023 winner City beat Porto 2-0. Madrid and City are expected to be among the main challengers to back-to-back defending champion Paris Saint-Germain this season and both will be relying on their star strikers. Mbappe's goal after 14 minutes was his 71st in European club soccer's top competition , and Haaland took his tally to 59 in 59 appearances in the Champions League. Borussia Dortmund beat Villarreal 3-2, and Real Betis won by the same score at Lille. Aston Villa also won 3-2 over Club Brugge and AEK Athens sealed a 1-0 win over LASK. PSG begins its campaign on Wednesday against Slovan Bratislava.

articles.title: Barcelona dances in the rain
articles.standfirst: Flick's team has continued its steamroller run in the Champions League, just as it has in LaLiga. They've scored 22 goals in five games. Raphinha scored twice and now has eight goals this season
articles.summary: Flick's team has continued its steamroller run in the Champions League, just as it has in LaLiga. They've scored 22 goals in five games. Raphinha scored twice and now has eight goals this season
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal scored with a free kick through the defensive wall as Barcelona beat Feyenoord 5-1 win Wednesday in its Champions League opener.

Raphinha extended his prolific start to the season with a fast goal inside three minutes in the early kickoff at Camp Nou. The Brazil forward added his second and Barcelona's third in the 57th.

Raphinha now has eight goals in just five games this season, as if sending a reminder to those who left his name off the Ballon d'Or nominations Tuesday.

Eight goals in just five games

Barcelona got high-class goals from all angles Tuesday, including from new signings Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus . Adeyemi found the top corner of Feyenoord's net with a precise curling shot in the 22nd and Jesus came off the bench to glance in a header in the 85th.

Teenage star Lamine Yamal fired a free kick left-footed from 20 meters (yards) in the 77th that went between two Feyenoord players jumping and turning sideways in the wall.

Feyenoord is coached by Giovanni van Bronckhorst , who returned to Camp Nou where he spent four years as a player and won the Champions League in 2006.

articles.title: Koke fervently defends Julian Alvarez after striker provides assist for Atletico Madrid in UCL
articles.standfirst: Alvarez looks to be regaining his top form, if his performance against Liverpool is a sign of things to come.
articles.summary: Alvarez looks to be regaining his top form, if his performance against Liverpool is a sign of things to come.
articles.body:
It wasn't quite the start to their Champions League campaign they envisioned, but Atletico Madrid certainly didn't embarrass themselves in their first match. Playing away against Liverpool at Anfield was always going to be tough.

Despite that, Atleti took an early lead, but couldn't hold on to it. They eventually lost 2-1 , but it was a very even game overall. Perhaps more importantly for Atletico Madrid, their much-maligned striker played well . After a chaotic summer that ultimately ended with him staying at the club he wanted to leave, Julian Alvarez delivered in his first start of the season.

Julian Alvarez gave assist and played very well in first Atleti start of the season

Alvarez provided the assist on Marcos Llorente's opening goal, then came very close to scoring a goal of his own from outside the box . He played all 90 minutes and finished the match with three shorts on target . Despite his strong game, many Atleti fans are still bitter about the situation - and apparently so are some journalists who cover the team.

Team captain Koke , for one, is sick of it. Following the loss to Liverpool, Koke made sure to leave things clear when it comes to the Alvarez situation: It's in the past and the team is moving forward with Alvarez ingrained in the squad .

Alvarez certainly ruffled a lot of feathers with his behavior over the past couple of months. His teammates probably didn't appreciate him wanting to leave, but they're standing beside him with the drama finished for the time being .

After all, the team sorely needs him. When he's in top form, he's a world class player . His game against Liverpool showed he's close to getting back to his very best.

articles.title: Raphinha and Courtois in the first ideal Champions team
articles.standfirst: The White goalkeeper features in the team thanks to his seven saves from the eight shots against Inter
articles.summary: The White goalkeeper features in the team thanks to his seven saves from the eight shots against Inter
articles.body:
UEFA announced this Friday the first ideal team of the 2026/2027 Champions League , whose opening matchday was played this week, and it includes three Spaniards, Marc Bartra (Betis), Pau Torres (Aston Villa), Ferran Torres (Paris Saint-Germain), one Barcelona player, Raphinha ; and one Real Madrid player, Thibaut Courtois .

'The first "team of the week", selected by the UEFA Technical Observers Group, consists of Thibaut Courtois (Real Madrid) in goal, Serginho Dest (PSV), Marc Bartra (Betis), Pau Torres (Aston Villa) and Archie Brown (Fenerbahçe) in defense; Martin Odegaard (Arsenal) and Martin Baturina (Como) in the creative area, and Michael Olisé (Bayern) and Ferran (PSG), Raphinha (Barcelona) and Ermedin Demirovic (Stuttgart) in attack.'

Courtois is included in the team for his seven saves from the eight shots he faced in Real Madrid's victory against Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabéu.

'Of Marc Bartra the report highlights that "Betis' defensive leader showed tactical maturity and dominance in the air, scoring two headers to help his team celebrate their return to the Champions League with a victory in Lille".'

' Pau Torres "had a significant impact at both ends of the pitch, making eight clearances —the most in the match— in his own area, while also creating four chances and providing two assists at the other end, helping Aston Villa prevail over Club Brugge".'

Raphinha, Barcelona's captain, "led the press with impressive intensity and made runs in behind to create danger from the back, as well as playing between the lines, topping off the performance with two magnificent goals" against Feyenoord (5-1).

'Ferran Torres "scored his first hat-trick with his new club, PSG, against Slovan Bratislava, drawing attention not only for his reactions in front of goal, but also for his excellent movement, which allowed him to be in the right place at the right time'"

articles.title: Lamine Yamal shines and leads Barcelona to victory in Istanbul
articles.standfirst: Barça struggled in the first half, but Lamine's stellar performance in the first 20 minutes of the second half led Flick's team to another rout. 10 wins and 43 goals
articles.summary: Barça struggled in the first half, but Lamine's stellar performance in the first 20 minutes of the second half led Flick's team to another rout. 10 wins and 43 goals
articles.body:
10 official matches and 10 wins. No other set of numbers better defines the trajectory of this Barcelona team, which has started the season in steamroller mode. In these matches, they’ve scored 43 goals. It doesn’t matter whether Raphinha—their best player on the field so far—is there or not, and they can even afford the luxury of not having a designated striker up front, as they did at Rams Park, since the goals just keep coming. They struggled more than expected in the first half after falling behind 1-0, but then Lamine’s masterclass in the first 20 minutes of the second half decided the match. Is there a limit to this team’s potential? Having survived the hell of Istanbul, two very tough away matches—against Betis and PSG—await them before El Clásico, and that’s where their true strength will be tested. If they come through those with flying colors, we could be looking at a season to remember for a long time to come.

Gabriel Jesus was expected to start in Raphinha’s absence, but Flick opted to deploy Dani Olmo—who is very popular in Munich—as a false 9. And the move paid off once again for the German coach. Barça controlled the ball from the start; the constant boos from the stands were music to their ears, and before the 20th minute, Gordon and Fermín had already tested Çakir. Rafael Leao and Osimhen barely saw the ball, and that was part of Barça’s success; they focused their attacks down Gordon’s wing, as the Turks tried to take Lamine out of the game with constant provocation. It was an impossible task: the Barça No. 10’s first touch was a measured pass to Dani Olmo’s head, but he just missed connecting cleanly.

Cancelo, who’s been scoring spectacular goals for a month now, tried his luck from distance and forced Çakir to make a spectacular save. Everything seemed to be under control for Flick’s team, but they were dealt a blow in the most unexpected way. Following a Barça attack that might have warranted a penalty on Gordon, the Turks launched a counterattack in which Leao outran Eric and crossed the ball back for Batrakov to finish—the shot deflected off Cancelo and caught Joan García off guard. The Turkish side gained momentum, and things could have been much worse, as just a few minutes later Yilmaz made it 2-0 off a corner kick that Osimhen had touched. But VAR stepped in, ruling that the Turkish player was offside.

The game took a complete turn, but just as the Turks were playing their best, the equalizer came on a shot by Cancelo off a low pass from Dani Olmo. Barça regrouped, and in stoppage time of the first half, Gordon had a chance to make it 1-2.

A dominant performance after the break

Barça came out determined to win the game in the second half, and just a minute in, Lamine set up a scoring chance for Gordon, who incredibly shot wide. Yamal continued to make sporadic appearances, but always posed a threat. And that’s exactly what happened five minutes in, when another precise cross—one that was very difficult to defend—was headed in by Fermín from close range to make it 1-2. Lamine was on fire and looked to make it 1-3 with a shot that sailed over the bar. With the Turkish team in disarray, Lamine pulled off an impossible play along the goal line—he was lucky with his first touch but managed to set up Gordon, who finally found the back of the net after numerous missed chances.

With the score in their favor, Flick took out Gabriel Jesus and Adeyemi. No big deal. And as soon as they both came off, another pass from Lamine led to a poor first touch by Gabriel Jesus, which set up Adeyemi to beat Çakir with a cross-goal shot. Lamine was taunted by the Turkish players in the first half, but their provocation only served to spur him on to put on a show in the second half, leading Barça to another rout. And the margin of victory could have been even greater had Adeyemi’s shot not been cleared off the line. The tenth victory for an unstoppable Barça: bring on the next opponent.

articles.title: Manchester United "sinks" in the midst of a civil war: "It's a fu**ing disgrace"
articles.standfirst: Lisandro Martínez's statements against the board have unleashed a full-blown Civil War at Manchester United
articles.summary: Lisandro Martínez's statements against the board have unleashed a full-blown Civil War at Manchester United
articles.body:
'Lisandro Martínez's words after United's 2-0 defeat to Atlético de Madrid have sparked a full-blown civil war in Manchester .'

His teammate Amand Diallo has described Manchester United's situation as "a fucking disgrace" , analysts define it as "a sinking ship" and legends such as Wayne Rooney , Jamie Carragher , Ashley Young or Paul Robinson lashed out at the Argentine defender.

'Amad Diallo: "It's a fucking disgrace, I have no words"'

Amad Diallo, Lisandro Martínez's teammate at Manchester United, posted a forceful reaction on Snapchat after the defeat against Atlético de Madrid.

'The footballer described Manchester United's current situation as a "fucking disgrace, I have no words" .'

Rooney calls for Lisandro to be punished for his criticism of Manchester United: "He had an ulterior motive"

Wayne Rooney, Manchester United legend, has harshly criticized Lisandro Martínez's angry reaction.'

The legendary striker accused the Argentine defender of having a "hidden agenda" during his post-match interview, in which Lisandro Martínez lashed out at the "Red Devils" board and manager Jason Wilcox .

I think what Lisandro Martínez did was very premeditated. Why does he give the interview right after this match? Did he offer himself up?

Wayne Rooney believes L isandro Martínez has risked creating more chaos in the Manchester United dressing room and disrupting harmony with his teammates.

"It's a complicated situation, because I was always someone who expressed what I thought when I was a player, and it's natural to want to give your opinion, but I think perhaps he has gone too far. That's something that falls to the coach and should be kept internal; the fans want to hear the players and see that they really care about the team," commented the 40-year-old former footballer on "Amazon Prime" .

To be honest, I don't think Lisandro Martínez has really managed to connect with the fans since he arrived, as he has suffered many injuries

Rooney stressed that "it’s clear that Lisandro Martínez cares and wants the club to invest more money and sign more players; although, to be honest, if that happens, I think he could be one of the first to leave because of his own performances. His level of play has not been good enough, but I think he is right in a way: the club needs to invest more both in attack and in defense".

The board has to analyze this issue with Lisandro and will probably have to take measures regarding it, because it is a lack of respect towards the whole club

"I think what Lisandro Martínez did was very premeditated. Why does he give the interview right after this match? Did he offer himself up? I rarely hear him speak. It seemed like something planned, something he had discussed with his team before making it public. It's sad, because when you need all the players to remain united, you can't go around airing what is happening in the boardroom. It seems to me that Lisandro had a hidden intention, because that doesn't match the performance. I think the performance was better... I also think it's somewhat disrespectful to his teammates, since he disrespects them by implying that they are not good enough," he pointed out.

Wayne Rooney insisted that "the board has to look at this and probably needs to take action on it, because it is a lack of respect toward the whole club. Yes, there are problems; everyone wants more players and better players, but these are the ones you have. As a player, you have to move on. You have to go out there and show why you are world champions."

"To be honest, I don't think Lisandro Martínez has really managed to connect with the fans since he arrived, as he has suffered many injuries. The truth is that I like him, I think he's a good player, but he has been injured; so, considering what Manchester United paid for him, he has not performed as expected. That said, I don't mean any disrespect; I simply think he has had a lot of injuries and hasn't played that much," he commented.

Jamie Carragher: "I think it's terrible that Lisandro Martínez came out and said that"

'Jamie Carragher, Liverpool legend and renowned television commentator, also spoke out about Lisandro Martínez's words against the Manchester United board.'

'When Lisandro says that "we had a fantastic season" last campaign... that was not the case; in fact, they sacked the manager. They finished third'

"They don't benefit anyone at all; now they will be the center of attention for the next few days because of this. No fanbase likes the executives or the bosses at the top, so United supporters will gladly swallow it and think it's great," he said on "CBS Sports" .

Lisandro Martínez has had a dreadful start to the season; dreadful, really bad

Jamie Carragher underlined that "I think it's terrible that Lisandro Martínez came out and said that. When he says that "we had a fantastic season" last season... that was not the case; in fact, they sacked the manager. They finished third because they did not play cup matches or European competitions, since they were knocked out of the cup tournaments very early".

"The reason they didn't sign players in the summer is that, in the four or five years he's been there, I think they've only qualified for the Champions League once. So, if every season you miss out on the Champions League revenue while Manchester United spends more than 200 million euros in the transfer market, sooner or later that has to stop, because the money isn't there. That's why the money Manchester United is shelling out this summer relates to players bought years ago; hence there are no funds available, because this can't go on indefinitely. It's a squad that has been through different managers and has performed terribly; tonight they played terribly again," he pointed out.

Carragher highlighted that "Lisandro Martínez has had a terrible start to the season; terrible, really bad" .

"Last season, Ruben Amorim lashed out at his superiors, and I immediately said they should fire him, and not just because of those comments. I thought: "You're lucky to keep your job; you can't start criticizing those above you." I believe a football club is a family and that many things happen within it: there are arguments, there are unhappy people... I can understand that he is not satisfied with the squad—or that Michael Carrick is not either—but the club as a whole must be taken into account," reflected the idol of the "reds".

'Ashley Young also criticizes Lisandro Martínez: "Players must take responsibility"'

'Ashley Young, another legendary former Manchester United player, echoed Wayne Rooney's words against Lisandro Martínez and confirmed that the Argentine's comments would complicate manager Carrick's situation in the coming days.'

'"Of course, it’s something the players talk about. Before the match we were saying that the club needed to invest more, but... they have invested in midfield, so what is it that he wants? For them to buy a completely new team? They’re not going to do that. They need to strengthen other positions. They could have signed players for the attack or the defense, but they didn’t. The match has just ended and emotions are running high; we understand that. But we know that signings have to work out and improve things; the club has to take its time to do it right," the former footballer commented.'

'Ashley Young believes that "the players need to take responsibility: "we are the ones who make up this team and this squad, and we are the ones who go out onto the pitch". They are the ones who have to perform and show what they are capable of. There will be no changes until January".'

'Paul Robinson: "I question the timing chosen by Lisandro Martínez"'

' Paul Robinson , former England goalkeeper, spoke on BBC Radio 5 Live about Lisandro Martínez's controversial statements: "I question the timing, with all the uproar currently surrounding Manchester United; a positive attitude needs to come out of the dressing room, but it is clear that they have not recruited well, that they need more players and that the squad is not strong enough".'

The Manchester United is a sinking ship

Jason Cundy has described this reaction from Lisandro Martínez as a "sinking ship" mentality, accusing the Manchester United players of selfishness for shifting the blame onto the owners instead of taking responsibility for a disastrous season.

At Sky Sports , they pointed out that players who publicly criticize the board, drawing parallels with Cristiano Ronaldo's case in 2022, usually do not last long at Old Trafford, especially considering that Martínez is currently in the final year of his contract.

Lisandro Martínez's words against Manchester United that have caused so much upset

'After Manchester United's 2-0 defeat against Atlético de Madrid, Argentine Lisandro Martínez pointed the finger at the Old Trafford offices : "You can't keep changing, changing and changing managers. What about other areas? Tonight it's easy to talk about the manager, it's easy to talk about the players, but we also have to look at other aspects".'

Now we expect more from the board, from senior management, to bring in more players to compete, because many teams have also signed many players

"We played a really poor match. Really poor. I have to control myself a lot, but sometimes it is a reflection of how our club is at this moment. I expect more investment. 100%. I expect more from our manager. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more, but it is also important, when you have a strong team, to be prepared for a night like this," said the Argentine on Amazon Prime .

Lisandro Martínez insisted on the idea that "we had a fantastic season last year and now we expect more from the board, from the top brass, so that they bring in more players to compete, because many teams have also signed many players".

articles.title: Güler Revives Mourinho's Madrid
articles.standfirst: Substitutions fix a disastrous game plan—lacking a midfield—with Vinicius struggling. From a 3-1 deficit in the 60th minute to a comeback capped off by three brilliant corner kicks from substitute Arda
articles.summary: Substitutions fix a disastrous game plan—lacking a midfield—with Vinicius struggling. From a 3-1 deficit in the 60th minute to a comeback capped off by three brilliant corner kicks from substitute Arda
articles.body:
R eal Madrid has an exceptional roster. This was evident in Rome, where the players underutilized by Mourinho turned around a major mess—a strategy of direct play without a midfield that allowed Roma to dominate. The Setúbal coach’s former team took a 3-1 lead, with Vinicius particularly off his game, and the desperate substitutions worked a miracle. Arda Güler delivered three perfectly executed corner kicks that were converted by Espí, Endrick, and Rüdiger—three goals in seven minutes to secure the win and offer several lessons. Soccer is played with midfielders, and when one player isn’t performing well, you have to make way for another who comes in hungry.

The uproar over Vinicius’s suspension and the controversy surrounding the referees took some of the spotlight away from the match in Rome, where Mourinho reaffirmed his status as “The Special One” by lifting a European title. For this special occasion—given the opponent and the Champions League, the eternal love of the Whites—the coach was bolder than ever. He started the BMV duo alongside Diomande for the first time. Such joy comes at a price, so he benched Arda Güler and stuck with the Tchouaméni-Valverde duo in the midfield. This dashed the hopes of many Real Madrid fans, who weren’t surprised by how the match at the Olimpico began. Roma, a team as daring as Gasperini’s Atalanta, exposed the Whites’ weaknesses.

Soulé had a chance 50 seconds in. Courtois made his first save at the 5-minute mark, stopping Hermoso’s spectacular shot right next to the post. Dybala fired Nahuel’s back pass wide; Nahuel is a left-footed wingback (12'). And Wesley took advantage of a defensive lapse to break into the box and . Of course, on the fifth attempt, the first goal went in. After Tchouaméni lost the ball on a clearance, De Roon’s long-range shot caught Courtois off guard after deflecting off a defender. It was the logical culmination of a dreadful stretch of play—no threat, no flow, unable to string together more than three passes, lacking focus on defense, and with no plan other than long balls, preferably from Courtois.

Perhaps Mourinho, cheered on by the Roma fans, had it all planned out. We shouldn’t rule that out. He did it before against Inter. But back then, he pressed and his team stayed compact with discipline. In Rome, he did away with midfield play, any build-up, and any attempt to create chances, in favor of seeking the decisive counterattack. Malen had a chance with a shot so hard it even startled Courtois, who was quick to prevent the goal. And on a loose ball, a long pass capitalized on Hermoso’s mistake, and Mbappé, on his first shot, scored the equalizer. The debate-ender.

Roma felt the impact of Real Madrid’s goal. They lost confidence in their full-field press and allowed Madrid to control the ball more. They were also hampered by the early injury to Koné, their anchor. Diomande stepped up his involvement, both with and without the ball. What a sight. A winger helping out on defense. It’s worth noting that the best chance before halftime came from a fullback playing as a winger, Cucurella, who capitalized on a mistake by Soulé and found himself one-on-one with Gollini. He finished it off with a mediocre right-footed shot. And Vinicius? Out of sync. Slow. His best moment in the first half was the back pass, just before halftime, that Bellingham sent wide.
